lesson.label: 📖 Bài học chính
lesson.title: 1. How an order goes through the company
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Minh has just started as a sales assistant at an electronics company. On his first morning, his manager explains what happens to an order.*
lines: Before you start, **let me quickly explain** how an order goes through the company, **from start to finish**. It'll help you understand **who does what**.
That would be great. I was **a bit confused by** all the different teams yesterday.
Don't worry, everyone is at first. So, **it all starts with** us in sales. When a customer **places an order**, you **enter** it **into the system** and send them **a price quote**.
Do I need to **get** the quote **approved**?
Only for big orders, anything over 50 million đồng. **In that case**, I need to approve it first.
**Once** the customer **pays the deposit**, the order goes to the finance team. They check the payment. You don't need to do anything **at this point**, but **keep an eye on** it.
How long does that usually take?
Usually a day. If it takes longer, just **give** finance **a quick call**.
Then the order **is passed on to** the warehouse. They pack everything and **arrange the delivery**. **As soon as** you get the delivery date, tell the customer.
So I talk to the customer the whole time?
Exactly. You're **the customer's main contact**. If there's a problem with the delivery, the delivery team will tell you, and you **keep the customer updated**.
**That makes sense.** Does anything often **go wrong**?
Yes. Sometimes orders **get stuck** because finance hasn't checked the payment. So **my advice is to** check your orders every morning.
OK, **let me just check I've got this right**: sales, approval for big orders, finance, warehouse, then delivery. And I keep the customer updated.
Exactly. Any questions **so far**? Just come and find me.

lesson.title: 2. Making Vietnamese coffee
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Tom is staying with his Vietnamese friend, Linh, for the weekend. In the morning, Linh makes cà phê phin and shows him how to do it.*
lines: Morning! Is that a coffee filter? I bought one last week, but **I've no idea how to** use it.
The *phin*? Yeah. What happened when you tried?
It **took forever**, and the coffee tasted like water.
Come here, I'll show you. **Start with** the condensed milk, about two spoons **in the bottom of** the glass.
Only two? I thought Vietnamese coffee was really sweet.
You can add more later. **Then** put the *phin* **on top of** the glass and add two big spoons of coffee. **Give it a little shake** so the coffee is flat.
OK. And this small metal thing goes on top?
Yes. Put it on **gently**. **Don't push it down too hard, or** the water **can't get through**.
Ah, that's my mistake. I always push it really hard.
**That explains** why it took forever. **Now**, **pour in** a little hot water, just enough to cover the coffee, and wait about thirty seconds.
Why can't I **fill it up straight away**?
You can, but it won't be as strong. **Trust me**, it tastes much better. **After that**, fill it **to the top**, put the lid on and **leave it to drip**.
Four or five minutes. If it drips too fast, push it down a little more. If it drips too slowly, it's too tight.
It's quite relaxing, just watching it.
**Yeah. When it's done**, **give it a good stir** and pour it over ice.
Mmm. That's much better than mine.
See? It's easy **once you know how**. You'll **get the hang of it**.

homework.title: Part 3: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to Ben's guide for new employees, then complete the flow chart.
homework.podcast: 🎧 What to do when your computer has a problem

script.text: Hi, I'm Ben from IT support. Welcome to the company! In this short guide, I'll explain what to do if your computer has a problem.
Step one: First, try turning your computer ==off and on again==. This fixes about ==half== of all problems!
Step two: If that doesn't work, open the ==IT app== on your phone and fill in a short ==form==. Describe the problem, and add a ==photo== of the screen if you can.
Step three: Once you send the form, you get a ==ticket number== by email. Please keep this number, because we'll ask you for it.

Step four: Someone from our team will contact you within ==two hours==. If it's an easy problem, we can usually fix it ==online==. If it's a bigger problem, we'll come to your ==desk==. And if we can't fix it the same day, we'll give you a ==spare laptop==, so you can keep working.
Finally, one tip: please save your work on the company drive ==every day==. That way, you won't lose anything if your computer breaks.
If it's really urgent, you can call us on extension 205. Thanks, and welcome again!
